column1: # kind slope: the ceiling is bytes of memory a row of the table, between the smallest and the largest size. SETUP, then WARM (`=`: the operation itself), run in a session of its own before the measured backend connects: the server holds the same whatever case ran before; a case on {f} or {d} warms, one on a copy ({m} {s}) is made new for each run.

# basis exact: the bytes the memory scopes of sift counted (sift._test_mem_highwater()), the same on every run and flavour; the ceiling is the slope measured on the release and on the tree plus max(2 B/row, 15%). The cases whose scopes count 3 B/row or more and most of the growth. basis sampled: the resident peak of the backend, for the cases whose scopes count none or a part of the growth (lookup_join_label: 53 of 165 B/row; the memory is PostgreSQL's or a table's, outside them); basis contexts: the leak kind, the bytes the contexts of the backend hold.

# status clean: the ceiling is at most 12 B/row (sampled: 3 runs under 10); open: a defect, the slope it was measured at plus its allowance (a fix turns the row to clean); noise: a sampled slope that moves between runs, the largest of 3 runs plus 15 percent, no floor. Open and noise rows say why in REASON.
# a row is added by its line: the columns after OPERATION may be left out for a clean case that needs no warm-up.
